test_title: PYST 9: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - GA (Held On 29 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: What is the primary role of the INSAT-3DS satellite launched under the GSLV-F14 mission?

options.text: To monitor India's defense satellite communication network.
To provide direct-to-home broadcasting services across rural India.
To enhance meteorological observations and aid in weather forecasting.
To serve as a backup for interplanetary deep-space communications.

solution:
The correct answer is __**To enhance meteorological observations and aid in weather forecasting.**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **INSAT-3DS** satellite is a follow-on mission of the third-generation meteorological satellite series from India, specifically designed to enhance **meteorological observations** and monitor land and ocean surfaces.

• Launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** on February 17, 2024, using the **GSLV-F14** launch vehicle, its primary objective is to provide continuity of services to existing operational satellites like **INSAT-3D** and **INSAT-3DR**.

• The satellite is equipped with advanced payloads, including a **6-channel Imager** and a **19-channel Sounder**, which are crucial for capturing high-resolution images and vertical profiles of the atmosphere (temperature and humidity).

• It plays a vital role in **weather forecasting**, providing data for **disaster warning**, and monitoring environmental changes across the Indian subcontinent and surrounding oceanic regions.

• The mission is fully funded by the **Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES)** to improve the accuracy of weather predictions and climate research.

**Additional Information__**

• The **GSLV-F14** is a three-stage launch vehicle featuring a **Cryogenic Upper Stage**, often referred to as the 'naughty boy' of ISRO in the past due to its complexity, but it has now achieved high reliability.

• The satellite was launched from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) SHAR**, located in **Sriharikota**, Andhra Pradesh.

• Apart from meteorology, INSAT-3DS carries a **Data Relay Transponder (DRT)** to collect data from automatic weather stations and a **Satellite Aided Search and Rescue (SAS&R)** transponder to assist in global search and rescue operations.

• The data generated by this satellite is extensively used by the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)**, National Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF), and the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS).

• This mission significantly boosts India's capability in tracking **cyclones**, monitoring **monsoon** patterns, and managing natural disasters.
